correctness.rationale: Exact finite-rank resolvent reduction: the positive spectrum of the selfadjoint point-interaction transmission operator is counted by eigenvalues greater than one of its zero-energy Green matrix. Strict Loewner monotonicity and decay of the shifted resolvent establish the index and nullity for arbitrary finite simple crossings. Direct differentiation of the isolated matching function gives the positive ratio G(s,s)/(G(s,s)-b′(s)), less than one on P and greater than one on Q. The full sourced separation estimates imply exponential convergence of the Green matrix to a diagonal matrix with strict gaps from one, yielding exactly the number of Q letters as positive eigenvalues. Existence of source profiles is explicitly attributed to arXiv:2610.32917v1. Replaying checker.py tests 40 sample profiles; it is corroboration only. Limitation: spectral transmission form, not nonlinear Fréchet stability.

Smooth small-topography Allen--Cahn prior literature is a relevant conceptual precursor but not the fixed jump-diffusion discontinuous McKean result. value.rationale: The source explicitly leaves spectral/nonmonotone multi-front stability unresolved; this theorem supplies a complete binomial Morse-index distribution on the actual new 2^m-configuration family and an exact finite-dimensional index criterion at any finite separation. It distinguishes one spectrally stable pattern from exponentially many unstable ones at fixed order-one diffusion contrast, with no numerical gap assumptions or extrapolated finite enumeration. This is structurally useful for bifurcation, instability and potential subsequent nonlinear stability work, while stopping short of asserting nonlinear stability.
